content: On Apple Silicon (arm64), macOS enforces that every executable have at least an ad-hoc code signature; unsigned or signature-invalidated Mach-O binaries are SIGKILLed (exit 'Killed: 9') immediately on launch by the kernel, even for a binary built locally. Any modification after signing (e.g. copying with a tool that strips xattrs, editing a plist inside the bundle, repackaging) invalidates the existing signature and must be re-signed with 'codesign -s - -f <path>' (ad-hoc) or a real identity. This is arm64-specific; Intel x64 does not require a signature to execute (though Gatekeeper/quarantine checks still apply for quarantined downloads).
